en: You know the core Bun features, you heard
about them, you maybe used them in some tiny
demo apps.
It's of course best to see them in a
complete realistic web app and that's
exactly what this section is about. In this
section, I'll show you in detail a complete
Bun demo web app, a social network web
application which includes authentication
using another library but powered by Bun
under the hood, of course. We'll use Bun's
web server and routing feature, Bun's SQLite
client for accessing a SQLite database for
data storage. We'll have images stored in
the cloud on Cloudflare R2, but we could be
using Amazon S3 too if we wanted to because
we'll be using Bun's S3 client. We'll have
automated tests and so much more. It'll be a
web application which requires
authentication and of course it also
supports account creation therefore.
And once you have an account, you're in this
basic yet fully functional social network
where you can follow other people,
where you can see the posts of people you
follow on your personal feed page, your
starting page,
you can like those posts, You can of course
also read them in full
and you can also share your own posts where
you can also attach images.
So that's the application I built and which
we'll now explore in greater detail in this
section. You'll find the finished project
attached so that you can play around with it
on your own.
There is a detailed README.md file in there
which contains more details about the
project, though of course we'll go through
it over the next lectures, but it also
contains detailed installation and setup
instructions instructions you should go
through
if you want to run this on your own because
you'll need to install dependencies. You
have 2 apps in there. I'll get back to why
and what these 2 apps are.
You need to set up a Cloudflare R2 bucket or
some other S3-compatible bucket which you
can use, and there are instructions for that
in here too,
and so on. So that is the way to go if you
wanna run this on your own. But of course,
now we'll dive in and see what exactly these
2 apps are about and which fun features
we're using here.
